summary: High 5xx/504 error rate on embeddings bulk upload following client retry amplification
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported elevated 5xx (predominantly 504) responses during a large embeddings bulk upload. Error rate started at ~14:22 UTC and persisted for ~45 minutes, coincident with a spike in retry traffic from the customer's client. Impact: multiple embedding jobs failed, delays for downstream inference consumers, and increased costs due to amplification.

Impact:
- ~40% of the customer's requests returned 504 during the window.
- Other tenants on the same Dedicated pool saw latency bumps but lower error rates.
- Business impact: delayed ML pipeline runs for Noteable Analytics (non-prod downstream jobs also affected).

Environment:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (shared GPU pool)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Customer: Noteable Analytics (dedicated tier)
- Affected models: text-embedding-3-small (primary), fallback embedding-1b-quant

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Customer ran a bulk embeddings upload: 24k texts in 200-file parallel multipart batches with client concurrency=200.
2. Several individual batch requests hit 30s client timeout and retried immediately with exponential backoff but effectively very tight (no jitter).
3. Retries amplified request rate to the API gateway and upstream runtime; queues filled and connections entered TIME_WAIT.
4. Serving runtime threadpool reached saturation and started returning 504s as requests timed out waiting for worker availability.

Relevant logs / metrics / traces:
- APIGW 5xx rate graph: spike at 14:22 UTC from 1.2% -> 38% for the customer's route (link: https://dash.redwood.ai/apigw/graph?range=1h&panel=5xx).
- Runtime busy workers: worker_util peaked at 98%, queue_latency increased from 12ms -> 620ms.
- Kernel socket backlog (netstat): SYN_RECV queue grew; ephemeral port exhaustion warnings in edge proxies.
- Runtime logs: repeated "worker threadpool exhausted" entries and "dispatch timeout - returning 504".
- Customer-provided client logs show repeated immediate retries (no jitter) after 30s timeouts.

Initial hypothesis:
- Client-side retry amplification combined with heavy multipart batching overwhelmed the gateway and upstream runtime.
- Runtime inability to shed load quickly caused queue growth and timeouts rather than graceful backpressure.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support requested that the customer back off concurrency to <= 16 and enable jitter on client retries (applied at 14:37 UTC).
- We applied a quick ingress rate cap for the customer's tenant on the API gateway (soft cap) at 14:40 UTC to reduce immediate pressure.
- Restarted two runtime workers on the affected Dedicated pool to clear threadpool leaks (rolling restarts 14:45–14:50 UTC).

Current state: partial stabilization as of 15:05 UTC. Error rate dropped to ~3% for the customer's route; background tail latency remains elevated while caches warm and connection pools recover.

investigation_notes: 14:25 UTC: APIGW trace shows hundreds of retries from the same source IPs; correlation with customer's upload job confirmed.
14:28 UTC: Runtime metrics indicate worker_pool.queue_length increased 50x compared to baseline; internal eviction policy not aggressive enough to shed excess requests before timeouts.
14:35 UTC: Edge proxy reports ephemeral port exhaustion warnings; increasing keepalive reuse would help but longer-term fix required.
14:40 UTC: Applied soft per-tenant ingress cap; observed immediate rate smoothing at APIGW layer.
Relevant links: APIGW dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/apigw/graph?panel=5xx; Runtime traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-embed-bulk
resolution_notes: Workaround implemented: advised customer to reduce concurrency to <= 16 and enable exponential backoff with jitter; implemented soft per-tenant cap and rolled two runtime workers to clear threadpool state.

Fix plan (short term): Adjust default per-tenant ingress soft limits for Dedicated customers who run large bulk jobs; add client best-practice guidance to Support KB. Assigned INT-4412 to infra to evaluate ingress default caps.

Fix plan (medium term): Improve runtime load-shedding behavior so requests are rejected earlier (503) rather than queued to timeout; add metrics to detect retry amplification patterns and trigger automated throttles. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2794.

Follow-ups: 1) Call scheduled with Noteable Analytics on 2026-03-12 to review recommended client configuration and discuss Dedicated pool sizing. 2) Post-incident postmortem to be written in Confluence and linked here.
